key_insight: The paper introduces an online memory mechanism for dynamic novel view synthesis that can remember long-term scene information without requiring expensive gradient updates at every frame. This makes test-time adaptation practical for real-time streaming video.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing temporarily occluded regions in dynamic multi-view videos while meeting strict real-time constraints. Standard test-time training methods are too costly because they update memory through backpropagation on every frame.
method: Uses an online neural space-time memory to store and retrieve long-horizon scene information across frames.
Adapts to changing motion in dynamic scenes more efficiently than standard gradient-based test-time training.
Reduces per-frame update cost so novel view synthesis can operate in streaming, real-time settings.
impact: This matters because it brings persistent memory and online adaptation closer to practical deployment in real-time vision systems. For practitioners, it offers a path to better reconstruction of dynamic scenes without the computational burden of full test-time retraining.
